pr_title: Bluetooth: Controller: Fix LE Set CIG Param handles returned
pr_body:
Fix LE Set Connected Isochronous Parameters Command Complete to return the correctly allocated Connected Isochronous stream connection handle instead of index of the iterator as handle.

Fixes #57904.
pr_comments:
> Please state the purpose of the change. What is the "fix"? The handle returned as iterator is the actual handle. If this is no longer the case, then `ll_conn_iso_stream_get` will not work.

CIS contexts are allocated from memory pool and after CIG remove they are allocated back in LIFO order. The CIS context handle are stored as `cis->lll.handle`, returning the iterator does not reflect the correct allocated CIS context.

> > Please state the purpose of the change. What is the "fix"? The handle returned as iterator is the actual handle. If this is no longer the case, then `ll_conn_iso_stream_get` will not work.
> 
> CIS contexts are allocated from memory pool and after CIG remove they are allocated back in LIFO order. The CIS context handle are stored as `cis->lll.handle`, returning the iterator does not reflect the correct allocated CIS context.

That's critical. I think we need to look for other places then - as mentioned - `ll_conn_iso_stream_get` relies on the linear relation between index and handle.
The implementation follows the pattern from ACL connections, where handles are fixed. Are we sure we cannot keep this pattern for CIS, and instead fix the way instances are returned?

In `ll_cig_parameters_commit`, the `cis->lll.handle` is assigned via `cis->lll.handle = ll_conn_iso_stream_handle_get(cis);` so how is it that they can be mixed up?

> In `ll_cig_parameters_commit`, the `cis->lll.handle` is assigned via `cis->lll.handle = ll_conn_iso_stream_handle_get(cis);` so how is it that they can be mixed up?

`ll_conn_iso_stream_handle_get()` uses `mem_index_get()` plus `LL_CIS_HANDLE_BASE` and that is correct. I do not see any mix up. As `mem_acquire()` is used to allocate, `cis->lll.handle` has the correct connection handle.

> Please state the purpose of the change.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/57904.

> `ll_conn_iso_stream_handle_get()` uses `mem_index_get()` plus `LL_CIS_HANDLE_BASE` and that is correct. I do not see any mix up. As `mem_acquire()` is used to allocate, `cis->lll.handle` has the correct connection handle.

Yes my point exactly. So how is it that the handle obtained from the index+offset is not correct?

> > `ll_conn_iso_stream_handle_get()` uses `mem_index_get()` plus `LL_CIS_HANDLE_BASE` and that is correct. I do not see any mix up. As `mem_acquire()` is used to allocate, `cis->lll.handle` has the correct connection handle.
> 
> Yes my point exactly. So how is it that the handle obtained from the index+offset is not correct?

LHS `ll_conn_iso_stream_get_by_group()` return `handle` which is the iterator, which is incorrect. RHS `cis->lll.handle` is the correct connection handle for `cis`-es allocated to a CIG.

You could run the tests developed here https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/57032 to reproduce the incorrect handles returned after a CIG is removed.

> `ll_conn_iso_stream_get_by_group()` return `handle` which is the iterator which is incorrect

The iterator _is_ the valid handle by design. The function returns the valid handle bound to the instance by the index + LL_CIS_HANDLE_BASE.
I think we should talk F2F, when would you have time for a call?
Please consider #58154 as possible alternative fix.

> > `ll_conn_iso_stream_get_by_group()` return `handle` which is the iterator which is incorrect
> 
> The iterator _is_ the valid handle by design. The function returns the valid handle bound to the instance by the index + LL_CIS_HANDLE_BASE. I think we should talk F2F, when would you have time for a call?

Contrary to your argument you are now in #58154 returning `cis->lll.handle` :
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/45eb028b4abdabc050f202882188e530a7fdfaa6/subsys/bluetooth/controller/ll_sw/ull_central_iso.c#L334

Which is correct now in #58154, do you still need a F2F call?

@Emil-Gydesen-Bose Would you test if #58154 is an alternative fix for your GMAP testing? (I will close this PR when you approve/confirm #58154)

> > > `ll_conn_iso_stream_get_by_group()` return `handle` which is the iterator which is incorrect
> > 
> > 
> > The iterator _is_ the valid handle by design. The function returns the valid handle bound to the instance by the index + LL_CIS_HANDLE_BASE. I think we should talk F2F, when would you have time for a call?
> 
> Contrary to your argument you are now in #58154 returning `cis->lll.handle` :
> 
> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/45eb028b4abdabc050f202882188e530a7fdfaa6/subsys/bluetooth/controller/ll_sw/ull_central_iso.c#L334
> 
> Which is correct now in #58154, do you still need a F2F call?
> 
> @Emil-Gydesen-Bose Would you test if #58154 is an alternative fix for your GMAP testing? (I will close this PR when you approve/confirm #58154)

My argument was not that it was wrong to return `cis->lll.handle`, but rather it is the same as the iterator handle, so if that change fixed something, things were not right...
In my code change `ll_conn_iso_stream_handle_get` is used to get the handle, which is the same way the iterator gets the handle.
I think we can do without the call if #58154 fixes the issue.

> @Thalley  Would you test if #58154 is an alternative fix for your GMAP testing? (I will close this PR when you approve/confirm #58154)

@cvinayak just did a trial run, and the CIS IDs are correctly set when using https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/58154

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Controller: Incorrect CIS ID transmitted to peripherals on reconnect
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If a central connects CIS to multiple peripherals, then the transmitted CIS ID seems to become incorrect when both CIS are disconnected and then reconnected. 

For example we are seeing
1) Central creates CIG with CIG_ID 0 with CIS_ID 0 and CIS_ID 1 (which gets handles 6 and 7 respectively)
2) Central connects CIS with handle 6 to Peripheral 1 and correctly sends `LE Connected Isochronous Stream Request` with CIG_ID = 0 and CIS_ID = 0. 
3) Central connects CIS with handle 7 to Peripheral 2 and correctly sends `LE Connected Isochronous Stream Request` with CIG_ID = 0 and CIS_ID = 1. 
4) Central Disconnects both CIS and deletes the CIG. 
5) Central creates the CIG with same parameters (i.e. CIG_ID 0 and CIS_ID 0 and CIS_1), and gets handles 6 and 7
6) Central connects CIS with 6 to Peripheral 1, but incorrectly sends `LE Connected Isochronous Stream Request` with CIG_ID = 0 and CIS_ID = 1. 

**To Reproduce**
See above

**Expected behavior**
After recreating the CIG and wanting to connect the CIS again, the `LE Connected Isochronous Stream Request` for handle should use CIS_ID 0. 

**Impact**
Breaking for TWS if attempting to reconnect the CIS

**Logs and console output**
See attached `btmon` files
[central.txt](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/11479676/central.txt)
[peripheral_1.txt](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/11479677/peripheral_1.txt)
[peripheral_2.txt](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/11479678/peripheral_2.txt)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Commit SHA or Version used: a13858e13278a82100541a98995caa8afe629808 but using a non-default Zephyr hex for the nRF5340 netcpu (
[hci_rpmsg_iso_zll_202305150947.hex.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/11479700/hci_rpmsg_iso_zll_202305150947.hex.zip) ) 

**Additional context**
N/A
